description: A nine-panel composite of TEM bright-field (BF) micrographs of deformation substructures arranged in three rows and three columns. The rows are the hot-rolling reductions (a–c) HR45, (d–f) HR68, (g–i) HR82; the columns are the interrupted-tensile engineering strain εe = 0.1 for (a, d, g), 0.2 for (b, e, h) and 0.4 for (c, f, i). Panels (a), (b), (d), (e), (g) and (h) carry 500 nm scale bars, while (c), (f) and (i) carry 1 µm scale bars. In the 0.1-strain panels white dashed lines mark {111} slip traces; in (a) and (d) two non-coplanar trace sets cross, forming a Taylor lattice. The 0.2-strain panels show more closely spaced slip bands, and (e) and (h) already carry white arrows with a "Microbands" label that (b) lacks. The 0.4-strain panels are labelled "Microbands", with hollow arrows marking ill-defined boundaries and solid straight lines marking distinct boundaries. Every panel shows dark dislocation walls/bands and dense tangles in a lighter austenite matrix; apart from the scale bars no numeric data are printed. Together the panels demonstrate that planar-glide slip bands refine with strain and then evolve into microbands, and that this transition occurs at a lower strain with increasing hot-rolling reduction.

TEM-BF micrograph of HR45 at εe = 0.4; label 'Microbands' with hollow arrows pointing to ill-defined band boundaries and solid straight lines marking distinct boundaries; 1 µm scale bar.
TEM-BF micrograph of HR68 at εe = 0.1; sparse individual dislocations and planar slip traces; crossing {111} slip traces marked by white dashed lines; 500 nm scale bar.
TEM-BF micrograph of HR68 at εe = 0.2; heavy dark dislocation tangles, 'Microbands' annotated with hollow arrows plus a white dashed {111} slip trace; 500 nm scale bar.
TEM-BF micrograph of HR68 at εe = 0.4; dense 'Microbands' with hollow arrows for ill-defined boundaries and solid lines for distinct boundaries; 1 µm scale bar.
TEM-BF micrograph of HR82 at εe = 0.1; dense dislocation network with closely spaced {111} slip traces marked by a white dashed line; 500 nm scale bar.
TEM-BF micrograph of HR82 at εe = 0.2; dark banded structure labelled 'Microbands' with hollow arrows and a white dashed {111} slip trace set; 500 nm scale bar.

observations.observation: The figure consists of nine TEM bright-field (BF) micrographs, three rows × three columns, showing deformation substructures of the austenite matrix.
Panels (a), (b), (d), (e), (g) and (h) each contain a 500 nm scale bar; panels (c), (f) and (i) each contain a 1 µm scale bar.

White dashed lines labelled "{111} slip traces" are drawn on panels (a), (b), (d), (e), (g) and (h); in (a) and (d) two non-coplanar dashed trace sets intersect, forming a grid characteristic of a Taylor lattice.

In panel (c) the annotation "Microbands" is accompanied by hollow arrows (ill-defined boundaries) and solid straight lines (distinct boundaries); the same annotation style appears in (f), (h) and (i), with (i) showing multiple solid lines.
Panels (e) and (h) (εe = 0.2) carry a "Microbands" label with hollow arrows, whereas panel (b) at the same strain contains only {111} slip traces and no microband annotation.
No numeric data values are printed inside any panel; the only printed numbers are the scale-bar lengths 500 nm and 1 µm.
The caption states panels (a–c) are HR45, (d–f) HR68 and (g–i) HR82, imaged after engineering strains of (a, d, g) 0.1, (b, e, h) 0.2 and (c, f, i) 0.4.
The caption states the images were taken along the 〈110〉 zone axis of the austenite matrix (printed without a closing bracket as "〈1 1 0 zone axis").

The caption states that dashed lines denote coplanar and non-coplanar slip traces of the {111} slip plane, arrows denote microbands with ill-defined boundaries, and solid lines denote microbands with distinct boundaries.
The citing text reports slip band spacings at εe = 0.1 of 296.40 ± 50.06 nm, 155.02 ± 38.42 nm and 68.05 ± 8.91 nm for HR45, HR68 and HR82 respectively (referring to Fig. 11(a), (d), (g)).
The citing text states that the slip band spacing barely changed once it reached ~50 nm, indicating saturation of slip band refinement.
The citing text states that microbands were observed at εe = 0.2 in the HR68 and HR82 samples, indicating faster substructure development than in HR45.
The citing text attributes the planar-glide substructures to "glide plane softening" caused by shearing of κ-carbides, despite a calculated stacking fault energy of ~73 mJ/m² for the steel.

measured_quantities: hot-rolling reduction (%) as sample designation HR45/HR68/HR82
spatial scale via scale bars: 500 nm and 1 µm
slip band spacing (nm) (values reported in the citing text, not printed on the panels)
unreadable_items: panel (a): a partially cut-off annotation at the bottom-left corner is not legible
panel (h): the "{111}" label overlaps the dark microband contrast and is only partially readable
no crystallographic indices (e.g. specific slip plane variants) are printed on any panel, so individual slip systems cannot be assigned from the pixels
